excerpt.en: As tools absorb more specialized knowledge, deep expertise matters less and fundamental critical thinking matters more. What's rising as memorized know-how falls.
excerpt.de: Während Werkzeuge immer mehr Spezialwissen aufnehmen, zählt tiefe Expertise weniger und grundlegendes kritisches Denken mehr. Was steigt, während auswendiges Können fällt.

body.en:
For most of my life, deep expertise was the moat: know more than the next person about a narrow thing, and you were valuable. That moat is draining. As tools absorb more and more specialized knowledge, being the person who *memorized the domain* matters less every year.

What rises as that falls isn't nothing. It's fundamental critical thinking — the ability to frame problems, judge answers, and know what question to even ask.

## What's actually depreciating

- Memorized know-how and lookup-able facts.
- Narrow procedural skill that a tool can now perform on request.

## What's appreciating

- Judgment: which answer is right, and right *for what*.
- Problem-framing: expertise tells you how; thinking tells you whether.
- Taste, and the ability to detect when a confident answer is wrong.

## The uncomfortable part

- This threatens the identity of people (me included) who invested in being The Expert.
- "Critical thinking" is easy to preach and hard to actually develop — I shouldn't hand-wave it.

## Notes to self

- Avoid the lazy "AI changes everything" framing. Be specific about what changes and what doesn't.
- Tie to the bespoke-problems post — same underlying shift.
